diagnostic_approaches.name: Malignant airway obstruction classification by airway involvement
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify malignant airway obstruction based on airway involvement
criteria_or_scoring: The vast majority of cases present with both tumor within the airway, intrinsic and external compression of the airway, extrinsic.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Malignant airway obstruction is often classified based on the airway involvement:

diagnostic_approaches.name: PITTS classification: simple vs complex
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify postintubation or posttracheostomy tracheal stenoses
criteria_or_scoring: complex (involving the deterioration of the cartilaginous rings)
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: PITTS are classified between simple (web-like) and complex (involving the deterioration of the cartilaginous rings) (Fig. 9).

diagnostic_approaches.name: Significant reduction in airway luminal diameter (>50%) criterion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify cases that may be an indication for a silicone airway stent
criteria_or_scoring: significant reduction in airway luminal diameter (greater than 50%)
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Any pathology with >50% airway luminal diameter reduction
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Any pathology leading a significant reduction in airway luminal diameter (greater than 50%) may be an indication for a silicone airway stent.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Temporary stent placement to test clinical improvement
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assess whether a patient will benefit from a stabilizing procedure
criteria_or_scoring: Clinical improvement after internal splinting indicates proceeding to external stenting
lack of improvement leads to stent removal and physiotherapy/CPAP
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Temporarily place an airway stent and evaluate for clinical improvement from internal splinting
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Improvement -> refer for external stenting; No improvement -> remove stent and recommend physiotherapy and CPAP
limitations: Procedure may shift the choke region toward the periphery
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Therefore, in a trial and error approach, it can be considered to temporarily place a stent and test whether the patient improves clinically from this internal splinting.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Intraoperative bronchoscopic measurement of lesion length
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Determine appropriate stent length to cover the airway abnormality
criteria_or_scoring: Stent should extend 5 mm above and below the abnormality
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use rigid optic or a flexible bronchoscope to measure lesion length intraoperatively
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Use measured length to choose a stent extending beyond the lesion by 5 mm proximally and distally
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Intraoperatively during stent planning and deployment
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Ideally, the stent should extend 5 mm above and below the abnormality.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Preoperative CT-based preliminary measurement of lesion length
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Estimate lesion length prior to bronchoscopy to assist stent planning
criteria_or_scoring: Preliminary CT measurements subsequently confirmed endoscopically
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Estimate measurements from CT images preoperatively and confirm endoscopically
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: CT provides a preliminary length estimate; endoscopy confirms before selecting stent length
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Preoperatively preliminary measurements can be estimated from the CT images and then confirmed endoscopically. Ideally, the stent should extend 5 mm above and below the abnormality.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Airway diameter estimation via rigid bronchoscope barrel size
criteria_or_scoring: Based on largest diameter rigid bronchoscope barrel utilized to maximally mechanically dilate the airway
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Mechanically dilate with rigid bronchoscope; choose stent diameter matching the largest barrel used
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Use dilation caliber to guide stent diameter choice
limitations: For fistulas and tracheobronchomalacia, oversize slightly to avoid migration
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During pre-deployment sizing after mechanical dilation
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: In stenotic lesions of the trachea, 14–16-mm stents are often selected.

clinical_guidelines.title: Indications Threshold and Major Indications for Silicone Airway Stents
clinical_guidelines.condition: Central airway obstruction
specific_recommendations: Any pathology leading a significant reduction in airway luminal diameter (greater than 50%) may be an indication for a silicone airway stent.
Major indications include: Counteracting extrinsic compression from tumors or lymph nodes.
Major indications include: Stabilizing airway patency after endoscopic removal of intraluminally growing cancer.
Major indications include: Treating benign strictures.
Major indications include: Stabilizing collapsing airways (malacia and polychondritis).
Major indications include: Sealing fistulas, e.g., stump dehiscences or fistulas between the trachea and esophagus.
decision_points_and_pathways: If airway luminal diameter reduction >50%, consider placement of a silicone airway stent.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: airway obstruction leading to the onset of debilitating symptoms such as dyspnea whether the obstruction is due to a malignant or benign process either intrinsic or extrinsic to the airway.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Any pathology leading a significant reduction in airway luminal diameter (greater than 50%) may be an indication for a silicone airway stent.

clinical_guidelines.title: Management Pathways for Malignant Airway Stenosis
clinical_guidelines.condition: Malignant airway stenosis
specific_recommendations: Purely intrinsic involvement can often be managed with debulking techniques.
A stent may be placed as a bridge to the response to chemoradiotherapy, when there is a high risk of local recurrence, or as palliative after failure of the oncologic treatment.
For patients’ naïve from any oncologic treatment, placement of a stent is not recommended.
Treatment of mixed disease is usually multimodality with debulking and stent insertion.
Extrinsic compression without intraluminal disease is readily treated with dilatation followed by stenting.
decision_points_and_pathways: Classify airway involvement: purely intrinsic vs mixed (intrinsic + extrinsic) vs extrinsic compression.
If purely intrinsic: perform debulking; consider stent as bridge, for high local recurrence risk, or after oncologic treatment failure.
If mixed: use multimodality treatment with debulking and stent insertion.
If extrinsic only: perform dilatation followed by stenting.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: The most common indication is malignant airway obstruction from a bronchogenic malignancy.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: For patients’ naïve from any oncologic treatment, placement of a stent is not recommended.
clinical_guidelines.outcome_measures: The stent has proven to be well tolerated in terms of quality of life.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: For patients’ naïve from any oncologic treatment, placement of a stent is not recommended. The stent has proven to be well tolerated in terms of quality of life.

clinical_guidelines.title: Management of Postintubation or Posttracheostomy Tracheal Stenoses (PITTS)
clinical_guidelines.condition: Postintubation or Posttracheostomy Tracheal Stenosis (PITTS)
specific_recommendations: Simple PITTS are generally not amenable to stent insertion.
Complex PITTS recur in about 70% after dilatation alone.
Dumon stents are suitable as they are removable and do not jeopardize a possible postponed surgery unlike metallic stents.
Migration can be reduced by the use of a dedicated hourglass silicone stent or by external fixation.
decision_points_and_pathways: Classify PITTS as simple (web-like) vs complex (involving deterioration of cartilaginous rings).
If simple: generally not amenable to stent insertion.
If complex: consider silicone (Dumon) stent placement; consider hourglass stent or external fixation to reduce migration.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Postintubation or Posttracheostomy Tracheal Stenoses (PITTS).
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Simple PITTS are generally not amenable to stent insertion.
alternative_approaches: FDA published recommendations for the use of nonfully covered metallic stents in this indication.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Simple PITTS are generally not amenable to stent insertion unlike the complex PITTS which recur in about 70% after dilatation alone.

clinical_guidelines.title: Management of Bronchial Stenosis Following Lung Transplantation
clinical_guidelines.condition: Anastomotic bronchial stenosis after lung transplantation
specific_recommendations: Select a stent that can be removed if necessary without causing further tissue damage.
The stents have been removed definitely in 70% of the patients without further recurrence.
The new surgical technique for bronchial anastomosis implies an anastomosis very close to the secondary carinas on both sides; this indicates bifurcated stents when a complication occurs.
decision_points_and_pathways: Choose removable stents to avoid further tissue damage.
When anastomosis is close to secondary carinas and complications occur, use bifurcated stents.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: anastomotic stenosis after lung transplantation
clinical_guidelines.outcome_measures: Definitive stent removal without recurrence achieved in 70% of patients.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The stents have been removed definitely in 70% of the patients without further recurrence.

clinical_guidelines.title: Use of Stents in Tracheobronchomalacia
clinical_guidelines.condition: Tracheobronchomalacia (malacias)
specific_recommendations: Most endoscopists have become reluctant about the use of permanent stent placement for malacias.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: malacias
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Therefore, most endoscopists have become reluctant about the use of permanent stent placement for malacias

clinical_guidelines.title: Temporary airway stent trial with decision pathway for suspected airway malacia
clinical_guidelines.condition: Malacic stenoses; flexible dyskinetic tracheas
specific_recommendations: Temporarily place a stent and test whether the patient improves clinically from this internal splinting.
If they do, send to the surgeon for external stenting techniques.
If not, remove the stent and recommend physiotherapy and CPAP.
The straight Dumon stent cannot be recommended for malacic stenoses; in flexible dyskinetic tracheas and gradually opening benign stenoses, it is prone to migration.
decision_points_and_pathways: Place temporary stent → assess clinical improvement → if improved → refer for external stenting.
Place temporary stent → assess clinical improvement → if not improved → remove stent + physiotherapy + CPAP.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Malacic stenoses; flexible dyskinetic tracheas; gradually opening benign stenoses
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Straight Dumon stent cannot be recommended for malacic stenoses due to migration risk.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: to temporarily place a stent and test whether the patient improves clinically from this internal splinting. If they do, they are sent to the surgeon for external stenting techniques.

clinical_guidelines.title: Airway stenting for tracheoesophageal or bronchoesophageal fistulas
clinical_guidelines.condition: Tracheoesophageal or bronchoesophageal fistulas
specific_recommendations: Placement of an airway stent can prevent obstruction from the esophageal tube and can help in sealing the fistula.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with esophago-airway fistula
clinical_guidelines.outcome_measures: Prevent airway obstruction; help seal fistula
alternative_approaches: Insertion of an esophageal tube (improves quality of life but usually fails to seal the fistula)
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Placement of an airway stent can prevent obstruction from the esophageal tube and can help in sealing the ﬁstula (Fig. 10).

clinical_guidelines.title: Management of bronchopleural fistulas
clinical_guidelines.condition: Postpneumonectomy or lobectomy stump fistula (bronchopleural fistula)
specific_recommendations: Surgery is the treatment of choice.
Endoscopic techniques, including placement of silicone stents, are an option when surgery is not possible or must be postponed.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Postpneumonectomy or lobectomy stump fistula
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Surgery is the treatment of choice of this condition but endoscopic techniques have been advocated as an option when surgery is not possible or has to be postponed.

clinical_guidelines.title: Contraindications and precautions for airway stenting
clinical_guidelines.condition: General airway stenting indications (malignant and benign)
specific_recommendations: In life-threatening situations, there are hardly any contraindications.
Other techniques should be used first before a stent is placed.
Intraluminally growing tumors should be removed first by laser resection, then a larger stent should be placed if still necessary.
Treating benign lesions requires particular caution; only removable stents should be used until a multidisciplinary team has determined inoperability.
Instability of the airways is not a contraindication but hardly ever a good indication for permanent stent placement.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Benign lesions; life-threatening airway obstruction; intraluminally growing tumors
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Permanent stent placement is hardly ever a good indication for airway instability.
alternative_approaches: Laser resection for intraluminal tumors prior to stenting
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In life-threatening situations, there are hardly any contraindications. However, other techniques should be used first before a stent is placed.

clinical_guidelines.title: Use rigid bronchoscopy under general anesthesia for silicone stent deployment
clinical_guidelines.condition: Silicone airway stent placement
specific_recommendations: Deploy silicone stents using rigid bronchoscopy under general anesthesia.
Rigid bronchoscopy is essential for insertion of Dumon stents as they are not auto-expandable.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: the deployment of a silicone stent must be performed using rigid bronchoscopy under general anesthesia.

clinical_guidelines.title: Pre-deployment tumor debulking and airway dilation
clinical_guidelines.condition: Silicone airway stent placement (preparation)
specific_recommendations: Use the rigid bronchoscope for mechanical tumor debulking and airway dilation prior to stent insertion.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: serves as a useful tool both for mechanical tumor debulking and airway dilation prior to stent insertion (Fig. 11).

clinical_guidelines.title: Stent length coverage guideline
clinical_guidelines.condition: Lesion coverage with silicone airway stent
specific_recommendations: Ideally, extend the stent 5 mm above and below the abnormality.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Airway lesions requiring stent coverage
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Ideally, the stent should extend 5 mm above and below the abnormality.

clinical_guidelines.title: Stent diameter selection for tracheal stenosis
clinical_guidelines.condition: Stenotic lesions of the trachea
specific_recommendations: Select 14–16-mm stents for stenotic lesions of the trachea.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Tracheal stenosis
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: In stenotic lesions of the trachea, 14–16-mm stents are often selected.

clinical_guidelines.title: Stent diameter selection for main stem bronchi and bronchus intermedius
clinical_guidelines.condition: Stenoses of the main stem bronchi and bronchus intermedius
specific_recommendations: Use 12- to 13-mm stents for stenoses involving the main stem bronchi.
Use 10- to 11-mm stents for stenoses involving the bronchus intermedius.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Main stem bronchi or bronchus intermedius stenosis
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The 12- to 13-mm and 10- to 11-mm stents are usually appropriate for stenoses involving the main stem bronchi and bronchus intermedius, respectively.

clinical_guidelines.title: Oversizing strategy for fistulas and tracheobronchomalacia
clinical_guidelines.condition: Fistulas and tracheobronchomalacia (no lesion for anchoring)
specific_recommendations: Oversize the stent slightly to avoid migration when no lesion exists for anchoring.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Fistulas; tracheobronchomalacia
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: there is no lesion to which the stent may anchor; therefore, in order to avoid migration, it is important to oversize the stent slightly.

clinical_guidelines.title: Avoid distal pushing of stent during placement
clinical_guidelines.condition: Pathologic airway during silicone stent placement
specific_recommendations: Avoid pushing the stent more distally due to risk of perforation.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Airway with pathologic lesion
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Distal pushing rarely advised due to perforation risk.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Pushing the stent more distally is rarely advised due to the risk of perforation at the level of the pathologic airway.

clinical_guidelines.title: Complete stent expansion using balloon or rigid instruments
clinical_guidelines.condition: Silicone stent that does not completely open upon deployment
specific_recommendations: Use a balloon catheter or rigid instruments (rigid scope or forceps) to complete stent expansion.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: a balloon catheter or one of the rigid instruments (rigid scope itself or the forceps) may be used to complete the expansion of the stent

clinical_guidelines.title: Annual reassessment and replacement of airway stents
clinical_guidelines.condition: Any indication for airway stent
specific_recommendations: Recommend annual reassessment and replacement of the stent until it is no longer indicated.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with an airway stent in place
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: we recommend annual reassessment and replacement of the stent until such a time the stent is no longer indicated.

clinical_guidelines.title: Management of stent migration
clinical_guidelines.condition: Silicone stent migration
specific_recommendations: Extract migrated stent under rigid bronchoscopy and replace with a more appropriately sized stent.
Percutaneous external fixation may reduce risk of migration.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with migrated silicone airway stent
clinical_guidelines.outcome_measures: Resolution of cough or dyspnea due to migration
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Percutaneous external ﬁxation has been proposed to reduce the risk of migration.

clinical_guidelines.title: Management of granulation tissue at stent margins
clinical_guidelines.condition: Granulation tissue causing obstruction at stent margins
specific_recommendations: Use mechanical or thermal means (laser, cautery, cryotherapy).
Replace the stent if necessary.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with granulation tissue at proximal/distal stent margins
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: mechanical or thermal (laser, cautery, cryotherapy) means should be considered. Replacement of the stent may also be necessary.

clinical_guidelines.title: Prevention of mucoid impaction in stents
clinical_guidelines.condition: Mucoid impaction risk in silicone stents
specific_recommendations: Maintain humidification via nebulization of sterile normal saline 2–3 times daily while the stent is in place.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with silicone stent in place
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: maintaining humidiﬁcation of the stent via nebulization of sterile normal saline 2–3 times daily while the stent is in place.

clinical_guidelines.title: Management of stents impacted with secretions/bacterial overgrowth
clinical_guidelines.condition: Stent obstruction associated with secretions and bacterial overgrowth
specific_recommendations: Remove and replace stents impacted with secretions associated with bacterial overgrowth.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Stents impacted with secretions and bacterial overgrowth
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Stents that become impacted with secretions most often associated with bacterial overgrowth should generally be removed and replaced.

clinical_guidelines.title: Preference for silicone over metal stents in benign disease
clinical_guidelines.condition: Stent selection for benign versus malignant airway disease
specific_recommendations: Silicone stents are indicated for most clinical indications, malignant or benign.
Metal stents should for the most part be avoided in benign disease.
Completely silicone-covered metal stents may be an exception.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Benign airway disease; malignant airway disease
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Avoid metal stents in benign disease (except fully silicone-covered metal stents may be exception).
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Silicone stents are indicated for the vast majority of clinical indications whether malignant or benign, in contrast to metal stents that should for the most part be avoided in benign disease.

clinical_guidelines.title: Techniques to preserve ventilation to lobes covered by stents
clinical_guidelines.condition: Endobronchial stenting that may cover lobar orifices (e.g., right upper lobe with Y stents)
specific_recommendations: Use fenestrations or add stents to distal limbs (Borgne Y) to preserve ventilation to covered lobes.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients requiring Y stents potentially covering lobar orifices
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: These include fenestrations or addition of stents to the distal limbs, Borgne Y.

technology_and_technique.topic: Dumon vs Polyflex silicone stents (technology comparison)
technology_and_technique.summary: Dumon is the gold-standard silicone airway stent; requires rigid bronchoscopy, has external studs to reduce migration, is easily repositioned/removed, and is available in straight, Y, and hourglass designs (hourglass useful for short benign tracheal disease). Polyflex (polyethylene threads embedded in silicone) has thinner walls yielding a better inner-to-outer diameter, adapts slightly better to hourglass-type stenoses, but has a smoother outer surface and sharper edges and therefore a higher migration rate than Dumon. Polyflex is deployed via a semirigid tube; modified versions with outer struts have been reported to reduce migration. No quantitative migration or complication rates provided.

Dumon stents are inserted through a dedicated rigid bronchoscope using a loading tool and pusher; they can be readily repositioned or removed with rigid forceps. On-site customization (e.g., creating a fenestration to ventilate a collateral bronchus) is feasible. Bifurcated/Y designs address disease at the main or secondary carina. Polyflex stents are delivered from a semirigid tube; operator skill/training requirements are comparable to Dumon. No procedural success/yield percentages reported.

technology_and_technique.topic: Imaging visibility for placement and follow-up
technology_and_technique.summary: Dumon stents incorporate radiopaque studs (barium sulfate with gold markers), and a transparent Dumon variant allows visualization of mucosa behind the stent wall while preserving radio-opacity. Polyflex stents include tungsten spots for radiographic visibility. These features facilitate confirmation of positioning and surveillance; no diagnostic accuracy metrics provided.

technology_and_technique.topic: Patient selection and indications for silicone stenting
technology_and_technique.summary: Indicated for central airway obstruction (trachea, mainstem, and select lobar bronchi) from intrinsic or extrinsic malignant or benign disease, and for coverage of airway fistulas to the mediastinum, pleural space, or esophagus. Hourglass stents preferred for irregular stenoses and short benign tracheal lesions. Sizes accommodate pediatric and adult patients. Specific selection algorithms, contraindications, and outcomes percentages not provided in this excerpt.

Polyflex stents have a higher migration rate than Dumon, likely due to smoother outer surface; Dumon’s external studs are designed to mitigate migration. Modified Polyflex stents with outer struts have been reported as successful to address migration. Quantitative complication or migration rates are not reported in the excerpt.
Other CE-marked straight polymeric stents include the Noppen (Tygon) and Hood stents. The excerpt provides no comparative effectiveness, safety rates, or procedural yield data for these devices.

Abstract
Since 1990 and the creation of the ﬁrst strictly endo-
luminal airway silicone stent, commercially available, by
Jean-François Dumon in Marseille, it became possible to
solve or palliate complex airway diseases that, previously,
could either be managed by difﬁcult surgical procedures
associated with high morbidity and mortality or lead to
patients’ death secondary to respiratory distress

Since that
time, other silicone and metallic stents have been
designed, but the Dumon stent remains the gold standard
in airway stenting

This chapter will describe the different
silicone stents, their indications, technique of placement,
advantages and drawbacks
